description: Improper input validation in Delphix Continuous Data connectors allows an authenticated user to execute arbitrary operating system commands on the staging or target host.
cwe: CWE-78 CWE-78 Improper neutralization of special elements used in an OS command ('OS command injection')

title: CVE-2026-8863
description: Multiple Microsoft-sigend UEFI SHIM bootloaders are vulnerable to SecureBoot bypass. An attacker with administrative privileges or the ability to modify the boot process could use one of the vulnerable shim bootloaders to bypass Secure Boot protections and execute arbitrary code before the operating system loads. Specific UEFI DBX update is required to block these vulnerable boot loaders.
cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature
CWE-354: Improper Validation of Integrity Check Value
credits: Thanks to Martin Smolar of ESET for discovering and reporting this vulnerability

title: Sandbox Escape in Ubuntu OpenJDK Packages via xdg-desktop-portal
description: A sandbox escape vulnerability exists in the OpenJDK packages provided in Ubuntu. The .jar MIME handlers installed by these packages execute files marked as executable when the mailcap package is installed. A compromised or malicious sandboxed application with access to the OpenURI portal via xdg-desktop-portal-gtk can write a malicious .jar file to the host file system, set its executable bit, and trigger the handler to execute arbitrary code outside of the sandbox environment.
cwe: CWE-20 CWE-20 Improper input validation

title: Undertow-core: undertow:http request smuggling via oversized chunk-size bit overlap
description: A flaw was found in the ChunkReader component of the Undertow HTTP server, which is used by WildFly and JBoss EAP to handle chunked transfer encoding. The issue occurs because the parser uses a single internal variable to store both the remaining chunk size and state flags. By sending a specially crafted request with an extremely large chunk size, an attacker can cause these values to overlap, tricking the parser into thinking a request has finished prematurely. This can allow a second, "smuggled" request to be processed out of sync, potentially bypassing security controls.
cwe: CWE-444 Inconsistent Interpretation of HTTP Requests

description: Wildfly's IIOP listener may permit deserialization of input streams before authentication is performed. An attacker who can gain access to the IIOP port may be able to construct and send malicious objects and achieve deserialization, if the target EJB allows untyped method parameters, and depending on the potential gadget chains available in the running classpath.

Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform 7
Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform 7
Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform 8

workarounds:
Restrict network reachability to the IIOP listener (default TCP port 3528) so that only localhost or authorized management networks can access it.

1. Restrict port exposure using firewalld:
```bash
firewall-cmd --permanent --remove-port=3528/tcp
firewall-cmd --reload
```

2. If CORBA/IIOP interoperability is not required by deployed applications, remove the IIOP subsystem using the JBoss Management CLI:
```bash
jboss-cli.sh --connect --command="/subsystem=iiop-openjdk:remove"
```

Caveats:
Removing the IIOP subsystem will break remote EJB invocations or external services that rely on CORBA/IIOP protocols.

Warning:
Applying firewall changes or removing server subsystems will disrupt active client connections and requires reloading the server configuration or restarting the JBoss EAP service to take full effect.

title: Wildfly-core: path traversal on wildfly domain controller
description:
A path traversal flaw was found in WildFly's domain mode
  implementation. The LocalFileRepository.getFile() and
  getConfigurationFile() methods in
  wildfly-core/deployment-repository do not validate that the
  resolved file path remains within the configured repository or
  configuration root directories. A remote attacker who has
  obtained the slave host controller secret or compromised a slave
  host controller can supply a crafted relative path containing
  directory traversal sequences (e.g., ../../etc/passwd) via the
  slave-DC wire protocol, causing the Domain Controller to resolve
  and serve arbitrary files readable by the DC process. This leads
  to unauthorized disclosure of sensitive information such as
  configuration files, keystores, and system credentials.
cwe: CWE-22 Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory

title: Io.undertow/undertow: undertow: http response header integrity issue due to character truncation
description: A flaw was found in Undertow, an HTTP server, within its HTTP response header writing path. The `writeString()` method performs a silent narrowing cast from 16-bit Unicode characters to 8-bit bytes when writing HTTP response header values. A remote attacker can exploit this by supplying specific Unicode characters in user-controlled input that an application places into response headers. This can lead to the truncation of these characters into ASCII control characters or special symbols, potentially resulting in limited integrity impact or information disclosure if the application does not properly sanitize user input.
cwe: CWE-681 Incorrect Conversion between Numeric Types

title: LIBPNG has a heap buffer overflow in png_set_quantize
description: LIBPNG is a reference library for use in applications that read, create, and manipulate PNG (Portable Network Graphics) raster image files. Prior to 1.6.55, an out-of-bounds read vulnerability exists in the png_set_quantize() API function. When the function is called with no histogram and the number of colors in the palette is more than twice the maximum supported by the user's display, certain palettes will cause the function to enter into an infinite loop that reads past the end of an internal heap-allocated buffer. The images that trigger this vulnerability are valid per the PNG specification. This vulnerability is fixed in 1.6.55.
cwe: CWE-122 CWE-122: Heap-based Buffer Overflow
CWE-126 CWE-126: Buffer Over-read

description: An unprivileged attacker can craft a user-space process with a malicious ELF binary containing an out-of-range sh_link field. When root-level dtrace attaches to -- or instruments -- that process (via dtrace -p , pid probes, or USDT), the ELF parser reads heap memory beyond the allocated section cache array without any bounds check. This results in an uninitialized/out-of-bounds heap read that can cause a NULL pointer dereference crash of the dtrace process (DoS), or -- depending on heap layout -- a read-then-use of a garbage pointer controlled by adjacent allocations, providing a foothold toward further exploitation in a privileged context.

title: jackson-databind: Array subtype allowlist bypass in BasicPolymorphicTypeValidator (allowIfSubTypeIsArray)
description: jackson-databind contains the general-purpose data-binding functionality and tree-model for Jackson Data Processor. From 2.10.0 until 2.18.8, 2.21.4, and 3.1.4, BasicPolymorphicTypeValidator.Builder.allowIfSubTypeIsArray() allowlists any array type based only on clazz.isArray(), without validating the array's component (element) type against the configured allowlist. A PTV built with allowIfSubTypeIsArray() plus an explicit concrete-type allowlist therefore still permits EvilType[] even though EvilType is not allowlisted. When Jackson deserializes the elements and no per-element type IDs are present, it instantiates the component type directly with no further PTV check, bypassing the allowlist. This vulnerability is fixed in 2.18.8, 2.21.4, and 3.1.4.
cwe: CWE-184 CWE-184: Incomplete List of Disallowed Inputs
CWE-184 Incomplete List of Disallowed Inputs

description:
In Eclipse BaSyx Java Server SDK versions 2.0.0-milestone-05 to 2.0.0-milestone-12, deployments using the MongoDB backend are vulnerable to an unauthenticated arbitrary file write through the AAS thumbnail API.




The AAS thumbnail upload path accepted a client-controlled fileName request parameter and passed it through repository file handling as both a repository key and, during thumbnail retrieval, a local filesystem path. With the MongoDB file repository, the supplied filename was treated as an opaque GridFS key and was not normalized or restricted as a filesystem path. A remote attacker could upload thumbnail content using an absolute or traversal-style filename, then trigger thumbnail retrieval so that the uploaded bytes were written to the attacker-chosen path on the server filesystem.




This could allow writing files anywhere the Java process has permission to write and may lead to remote code execution. The default InMemory backend is not affected by this specific path because it normalizes and restricts file paths to its temporary directory.




The issue is fixed in Eclipse BaSyx Java Server SDK 2.0.0-milestone-13.
cwe: CWE-22 CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
CWE-73 CWE-73: External Control of File Name or Path

While the vulnerability is in Oracle Coherence, attacks may significantly impact additional products (scope change).  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized creation, deletion or modification access to critical data or all Oracle Coherence accessible data as well as  unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle Coherence accessible data. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 9.6 (Confidentiality and Integrity impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N).

description: Vulnerability in Oracle Java SE (component: Installation).  Supported versions that are affected are Oracle Java SE: 8u491 and  8u491-perf. Difficult to exploit vulnerability allows low privileged attacker with logon to the infrastructure where Oracle Java SE executes to compromise Oracle Java SE.  Successful attacks require human interaction from a person other than the attacker. Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in takeover of Oracle Java SE. Note: This vulnerability can be exploited by using APIs in the specified Component, e.g., through a web service which supplies data to the APIs. title: Undertow-core: undertow: websocketcontainer defaults for buffers and timeouts are infinite
description: Undertow is a flexible performant web server used in JBoss EAP and WildFly. A flaw was found in how Undertow handles WebSocket connections. Specifically, certain configuration limits like message buffer sizes and session timeouts cannot be adjusted and default to being unlimited. This allows a remote attacker to send large amounts of data or maintain connections indefinitely, potentially crashing the server by exhausting its memory or other resources.
cwe: CWE-770 Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

workarounds:
To mitigate this flaw, restrict access to the IIOP service (TCP port 3528) to trusted networks using firewall rules, or disable the IIOP subsystem if CORBA is not required by deployed applications.

To restrict or remove external access to port 3528 using firewalld:
```
firewall-cmd --permanent --remove-port=3528/tcp
firewall-cmd --reload
```

Warning: Reloading the firewall configuration may briefly interrupt network traffic. If removing the iiop-openjdk subsystem from the JBoss EAP configuration (standalone.xml or domain.xml), a full server restart is required, causing temporary service downtime.

Caveats: Blocking port 3528 or disabling the IIOP subsystem will prevent legitimate remote clients from communicating over IIOP/CORBA

title: Org.wildfly.core: wildfly: path traversal in take-snapshot discloses the server configuration to the monitor role
description: A flaw was found in WildFly. A user with the `Monitor` role, which is the lowest standard Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) role, can exploit a path traversal vulnerability in the `take-snapshot` operation. By manipulating the `name` parameter, this user can write a copy of the server configuration to an arbitrary location. This allows the `Monitor` role to read back the server configuration, including sensitive credentials, which would otherwise be restricted by RBAC, leading to information disclosure.
cwe: CWE-22 Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory

title: Wildfly-core: wildfly-core: deployer rbac role privilege escalation via path traversal in deployment name
description: A flaw was found in the ContentRepositoryImpl.copyExplodedContent function of the wildfly-core library, which is used by WildFly and JBoss EAP to manage server deployments. The issue occurs when the library processes an unsanitized deployment name. Due to a missing containment check, an attacker with the Deployer RBAC role can use path traversal sequences to access files outside the restricted deployment directory. This can allow the attacker to delete arbitrary directories or create files with arbitrary content, leading to a full privilege escalation to the management SuperUser role.
cwe: CWE-22 Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory

title: Resteasy-core: resteasy: corsfilter reflects arbitrary origin with credentials under wildcard config
description: A flaw was found in RESTEasy's CorsFilter, which, when configured to allow all origins ("*"), reflects the request's Origin header back in the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response together with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. This permissive cross-origin policy allows a malicious website to make credentialed cross-origin requests and read authenticated responses from a victim's session, resulting in a loss of confidentiality.
cwe: CWE-346 Origin Validation Error
CWE-942 CWE-942 Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

title: Resteasy-core: resteasy: iioimageprovider unbounded image decode (decompression-bomb dos)
description: A flaw was found in RESTEasy's IIOImageProvider, which decodes attacker-supplied image request bodies without enforcing any limit on the declared image dimensions or pixel count. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can send a small crafted image declaring enormous dimensions to trigger a very large memory allocation, exhausting the JVM heap and resulting in a denial of service.
cwe: CWE-409 Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification)

title: Undertow: undertow: chunkreader message length permits chunk-size overflow
description: A flaw was found in the ChunkReader component of the Undertow web server, which is used to handle chunked transfer encoding in HTTP requests. The issue occurs because a security check for the chunk size is performed before the value is shifted, allowing a specifically crafted 15-digit chunk size to bypass the limit and overflow into internal state flags. This can cause the server to terminate a request body prematurely and interpret the remaining data as a separate, smuggled request.
cwe: CWE-444 Inconsistent Interpretation of HTTP Requests

description: A flaw was found in io.netty/netty-codec-memcache. The Memcache binary protocol codec incorrectly reads `keyLength` and `extrasLength` as signed Java types instead of unsigned, as specified by the protocol. A remote attacker, if an application routes untrusted input into this field, can embed CR/LF characters to inject arbitrary SMTP commands. title: Keycloak-core: keycloak-core: saml adapter does not bind signed assertions to the configured identity provider issuer
description: A flaw was found in the SAML adapter component of Keycloak, which is used to secure applications with SAML-based authentication. The adapter fails to verify that the issuer of a signed SAML assertion matches the expected identity provider configured for the application. If multiple identity providers share the same trusted signing key, an attacker who controls one of those providers can create a validly signed assertion to log into the application as any user, potentially gaining full administrative control.
cwe: CWE-347 Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

description: A flaw was found in FreeType, specifically within its CID font loader. This can result in a denial of service (DoS) for the application or service processing the font, potentially causing it to hang or terminate.

title: Org.keycloak/keycloak-admin-cli: keycloak-admin-cli: kcadm custom truststore accepts arbitrary self-signed certificates
description: A flaw was found in the Keycloak Admin CLI kcadm tool, which is used by administrators to manage Keycloak servers from the command line. When a custom truststore is provided to verify the server identity, the tool incorrectly accepts any self-signed certificate as long as the hostname matches. This allows a network attacker to impersonate the Keycloak server, steal administrative credentials, and perform unauthorized management actions.
cwe: CWE-295 Improper Certificate Validation

While the vulnerability is in Oracle Partner Management, attacks may significantly impact additional products (scope change).  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized creation, deletion or modification access to critical data or all Oracle Partner Management accessible data as well as  unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle Partner Management accessible data and unauthorized ability to cause a partial denial of service (partial DOS) of Oracle Partner Management. title: Undertow: undertow: pathresourcemanager safepaths check allows sibling-directory symlink traversal
description: A flaw was found in the PathResourceManager component of the Undertow web server. This component is responsible for serving static files from the file system. The issue occurs because the mechanism used to verify if a symbolic link points to a safe location only checks if the target path starts with a specific string, without ensuring it matches a full directory name. This could allow an attacker to access files in a sibling directory if that directorys name starts with the same characters as an authorized safe directory.
cwe: CWE-22 Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory

title: Wildfly: wildfly-iiop: wildfly-ejb3: wildfly: authentication bypass on iiop ejb invocations as csiv2 ittprincipalname accepted without transport binding
description: A flaw was found in Wildfly. A remote attacker can bypass authentication on IIOP EJB invocations as the CSIv2 security interceptor accepts ITTPrincipalName identity assertions in the service context without verifying transport-level authentication, allowing a pre-auth attacker on the port 3528 to impersonate any principal on every IIOP-exposed @Remote EJB.
cwe: CWE-829 Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere

workarounds:
To mitigate this vulnerability without modifying binaries, apply one or more of the following operational and configuration controls:

1. Maintain or revert caller propagation to the default 'none' setting in the IIOP subsystem configuration:
Run the following management CLI command:
`/subsystem=iiop-openjdk:write-attribute(name=caller-propagation,value=none)`
Ensure that application deployment descriptors (such as jboss-ejb3.xml) do not explicitly override caller propagation to 'supported'.

2. Restrict network reachability:
Block external access to the CORBA/IIOP port (default TCP port 3528) using firewall rules, or restrict access strictly to trusted application networks:
`firewall-cmd --remove-port=3528/tcp --permanent && firewall-cmd --reload`

3. Enforce transport-level security:
If caller propagation is required for your architecture, configure the IIOP subsystem to require SSL/TLS with client certificate authentication by setting `server-requires-ssl="true"`, or enforce mandatory authentication via the `as-context` configuration.

Caveats:
Disabling caller propagation prevents client security identity forwarding across remote IIOP EJB calls, which may impact applications relying on distributed identity propagation. Restricting firewall access will prevent external clients outside authorized networks from connecting to IIOP services.

Warning:
Applying configuration changes via the JBoss management CLI requires reloading the runtime service (`:reload`), which will temporarily interrupt active client connections.
